description: sign(MBT close-to-close return on day t) -> LONG/SHORT target at target's day t+1 open, exit at day t+1 close. Split by whether the target execution day is a Monday (crypto's weekend gap, the one place in this project's data where a genuinely 24/7 market's non-trading-day information shows up) vs any other weekday, to test whether the weekend specifically carries more cross-asset signal than an ordinary day.
data_quality_note: 281/364 MBT daily bars have open==close (stale marks, same pattern as MCL's older history -- newer, thinner-liquidity product). Does not affect this test: only MBT's close-to-close return is used as the leader signal (verified genuine, only 3/363 days repeat the prior close), and target instruments' own bars are already known clean.
instrument_spec_caveat: MBT contract specs (0.1 BTC multiplier, not independently re-verified from a primary CME source -- network egress blocked) are NOT used here since MBT is only a signal source, never traded; only the already-verified target instrument specs (MES/MGC/MCL) are used for P&L.

mcl_data_quality_followup.trigger: MBT->MCL full-window base scenario showed an implausible 3.9% win rate in the first half of a chronological split-sample check
mcl_data_quality_followup.diagnosis: MCL's pre-2025-12-26 daily bars are mostly stale (open==close), already documented in H009/depth_assessment.json; since this engine executes the target on its own open-to-close (intraday hold), most 'trades' in that window have zero gross P&L and lose only the cost -- explaining the abnormal win rate

corrected_rerun.restriction: MCL target bars restricted to >= 2025-12-26 (independently established clean-window start from H009, not fit to this result)
corrected_rerun.conclusion: negative relationship survives on verified-clean data, weaker than the inflated pooled full-window number (t=-2.06 base) but still directionally consistent and moderately significant

first_half.note: overlaps almost entirely with MCL's known-stale window -- not trustworthy on its own

second_half.note: overlaps almost entirely with MCL's clean window -- consistent with the corrected re-run above

h013_followup_correction.summary: H013 (same session) tested the inverse direction and decomposed P&L by long/short side. Finding: this MBT->MCL result is substantially explained by MCL's own strong directional drift over the clean window (buy-and-hold +$4250) interacting with the original signal's short-heavy trade balance (94 short / 82 long) -- shorts alone lost -$3110, longs alone were +$795. Most likely beta exposure, not a genuine BTC->MCL information relationship. See reports/backtests/H013_INVERSE_BTC_MCL.json and hypothesis_ledger.csv H013 for the full diagnostic.
h013_followup_correction.confidence_revision: substantially downgraded from the original writeup in this file
